strings.title: A Match Without Spectators
strings.hint: A player died in a locked dressing room during the second half… who left the field for a few minutes without appearing in the match broadcast?
strings.solvedText:
The culprit: team sports physician Walid Nouman.

The star player had discovered that the doctor was involving players in banned performance-enhancing drugs for a betting network. He refused to participate and threatened to expose it. During the second half, the player feigned an injury and went to the dressing room. The doctor followed him, the only person permitted to leave the substitutes' bench without attracting attention. He injected the player with a substance that stopped his heart and mimicked natural exhaustion, then locked the room and returned to the bench. The broadcast did not capture his brief absence.
strings.summary.text: During a decisive match played without spectators, team star Yasser Qandil collapsed and died in the locked dressing room during the second half. It appeared to be a heart attack in an exhausted athlete. But analysis revealed an injected substance that stopped his heart. The room was locked and the stadium had no spectators, so every moving person appeared in the camera coverage… except someone entitled to move without suspicion.

strings.summary.victim.name: Yasser Qandil

strings.scene.intro: A match without spectators: everyone present is accounted for and filmed. The dressing room is locked with the victim inside. A tiny injection mark behind the knee is hard to notice. Only the medical staff can move between the bench and the room without attracting attention.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: The empty stands and stadium lights
strings.scene.notes[0]: An injected substance stopped the heart — injection behind the knee
strings.scene.notes[2]: A stadium without spectators — everyone is filmed
strings.scene.notes[3]: The victim refused involvement in doping and threatened exposure
strings.evidence[0].title: Injection Site
strings.evidence[0].desc: A tiny puncture, difficult to see. An injected substance stopped his heart, mimicking exhaustion.
strings.evidence[1].title: Medical Staff Bag
strings.evidence[1].desc: A vial of heart medication is missing. Only the doctor controls its contents.
strings.evidence[2].title: Camera Coverage
strings.evidence[2].desc: Shows the doctor leaving his seat in minute 58 toward the tunnel, then returning. He was the only person who moved without participating in play.
strings.evidence[3].title: Dressing Room Key
strings.evidence[3].desc: He holds a copy of the room key, which he justifies as being for "medical emergencies."
strings.evidence[4].title: Doping Messages
strings.evidence[4].desc: The victim's messages: "I won't take what you're giving me. I'll tell the federation everything."
strings.suspects[0].name: Coach Samir
strings.suspects[0].alibi: "I was on the touchline directing the team. The broadcast films me the whole time."
strings.suspects[0].statement: Yasser was the pillar of my team. His death costs me the championship. We disagreed over his position on the field, an everyday tactical dispute. I never left the touchline for a moment. A hundred cameras can confirm it.
strings.suspects[1].name: Walid Nouman
strings.suspects[1].alibi: "I went to the tunnel to fetch equipment. One minute."
strings.suspects[1].statement: My job is to protect the players' health, not harm them. I went to the tunnel for bandages, a routine errand. The doping allegations are slander that destroys my reputation. Yasser was exhausted and his heart failed. It happens to athletes, and I'm the first to grieve.
strings.suspects[2].name: Fahd, the Rival Player
strings.suspects[2].relation: Wants the victim's place in the starting lineup
strings.suspects[2].alibi: "I was on the substitutes' bench for the entire half. The camera was on me."
strings.suspects[2].statement: Yes, I wanted his place in the lineup. Every substitute dreams of that. But I stayed on the bench throughout the match, as the broadcast proves. My teammate's death is not my path into the starting team. It's a nightmare.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Equipment Manager
strings.witnesses[0].statement: Doctor Walid passed through the tunnel toward the dressing room in minute 58, not toward the equipment store as he claimed. He returned minutes later without bandages.
strings.witnesses[1].name: Broadcast director
strings.witnesses[1].statement: In a match without spectators, every movement shows. The only person who left the bench for the tunnel during play was from the medical staff. We recorded it because it caught my attention.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Anti-Doping Official
strings.witnesses[2].statement: Days before the match, we received a vague report of suspected doping within the team from an unknown number. It later turned out to be the victim's phone.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Death Notification
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: A player's death in the dressing room during the match was reported. Play was stopped and the room cordoned off.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic medicine
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Toxicology report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: An injected substance stopped the heart and mimicked exhaustion. A puncture was found behind the left knee. Death occurred around minutes 58–62.
strings.folders[2].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Broadcast Analysis
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: Review of all cameras: the only person who moved toward the tunnel during play was the doctor, in minute 58.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Medical Bag Examination
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: A vial of heart medication is missing from the bag, with no record of its use in the match report.
strings.folders[3].name: Interviews
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Doctor Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: The equipment manager and footage contradict his claim of "fetching bandages." He could not explain the missing vial.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Coach Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: The broadcast documents his presence on the touchline throughout the match.
strings.folders[3].docs[2].title: Rival Interview
strings.folders[3].docs[2].body: The camera documents his remaining on the substitutes' bench.
strings.folders[4].name: Confidential files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Doping Network File
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: The doctor was part of a network involving players in doping for betting purposes. The victim refused and threatened exposure.
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Confession Record
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: Confronted with the footage, missing vial, and messages, the doctor confessed: "He was going to bring down the entire network… and me with it."
strings.reports[0].title: Locked Location Report
strings.reports[0].author: Investigation team
strings.reports[0].body: A locked room plus a stadium without spectators means a closed, filmed group. Only the doctor had both the key and freedom of movement.
strings.reports[1].title: Motive Report
strings.reports[1].author: Assigned investigator
strings.reports[1].body: The victim's threat to expose the doping network provides a direct motive for the implicated doctor.
strings.notes[0].text: A stadium without spectators = everyone on camera… except someone entitled to move
strings.notes[1].text: Who holds the room key and can move freely through the tunnel?
